description: Some family offices hire primarily through referrals rather than public job postings
Recruiters may withhold the client's identity until trust is established
A family may hire a banker or adviser who has already served them for years
Known judgment and discretion can matter more than public personal branding
Many roles lack obvious public entry points or standardized application paths
Professionals often enter after years in banking, accounting, law, private equity, or investment banking
Candidates may need to become known within the professional network before opportunities emerge

dynamic: High cost of a bad hire
description: Access to wealth, documents, travel, homes, and family life raises the downside of hiring mistakes
